content.summary: Enoch grounds moral objectivity in stance-independent facts and ordinary deliberation, while confronting rival-package, noncognitivist, and reflective-anomaly challenges to action guidance.

representativeQuote.text: you've come to the conclusion that you ought to do it
representativeQuote.context: Enoch uses the first-person perspective to argue that reaching an ought-conclusion normally completes deliberation, even though weakness of will may still prevent action.

pro-ordinary-stance-independence.words: Ordinary judgments that humiliation is wrong present that wrongness as independent of anyone's preferences, social conventions, beliefs, or practices.
pro-ordinary-stance-independence.critique: Strongest feature: The everyday humiliation example sharply separates moral wrongness from personal liking, communal convention, counterfactual belief, and prevailing practice, while the explicit qualification prevents this discourse premise from pretending already to demonstrate a complete realist metaphysics. Principal limitation: Illustrative linguistic evidence cannot establish how consistently ordinary speakers understand moral claims, and independence from familiar stances does not alone identify robust normative facts as the uniquely adequate explanation. Live burden: The argument must connect this carefully bounded characterization of ordinary objectivity to an affirmative ontology while answering the possibility that another theory could preserve the same independence. Locked score: The very strong band reflects excellent conceptual precision, direct contact with a central bridge, and disciplined calibration, tempered by limited empirical breadth and an intentionally incomplete realist inference.

pro-deliberative-indispensability.words: Normative truths are indispensable to the respectable project of practical deliberation, analogously to explanatory posits, and thereby acquire ontological respectability.
pro-deliberative-indispensability.critique: Strongest feature: The analogy between explanatory inquiry and practical deliberation supplies an affirmative route to normative ontology, treating deliberation as a respectable project whose indispensable commitments deserve recognition rather than merely deriving realism from ordinary linguistic appearances. Principal limitation: The compressed comparison with electrons leaves the operative kind of indispensability underexplained, and it does not establish why indispensability within a practical project is sufficient for ontological commitment rather than usefulness inside that project. Live burden: The argument must defend the parity between explanatory and deliberative indispensability while showing that normative facts do indispensable work that rival attitude-centered or deflationary accounts cannot reproduce. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects high central relevance and a clear constructive mechanism, moderated by an analogy whose sufficiency claim remains somewhat stronger than its presented warrant.

pro-generalized-package-challenge.words: Because the rival-package objection generalizes throughout normativity and generates repeated higher-order questions, its apparent deliberative gap may depend on a false presupposition.
pro-generalized-package-challenge.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly contests the rival-package objection at its governing level, using unrestricted generalization and repeated higher-order iteration to motivate the calibrated suspicion that the supposed residual question may arise from a defective framing rather than genuine deliberative incompleteness. Principal limitation: The speaker expressly cannot identify the alleged false presupposition, so generality and iteration remain diagnostic clues instead of a criterion showing why the opposing question is unintelligible or illegitimate. Live burden: The response must distinguish harmless repetition from substantive regress and explain what licenses deliberative closure without merely redescribing the recurring challenge as a pseudo-problem. Locked score: The strong and competent band recognizes decisive relevance, candid uncertainty, and substantial responsiveness, while withholding stronger evaluation because the central defeating premise is asserted conditionally but never specified.

pro-normative-metaphysical-privilege.words: Metaphysical privilege may itself be normative, and renewed questions about privilege versus privilege-star repeat the original purported pseudo-problem rather than advancing it.
pro-normative-metaphysical-privilege.critique: Strongest feature: The response squarely chooses the normative horn of the privilege dilemma, clarifies that normativity can fall within metaphysics, and accurately identifies the higher-order privilege-versus-privilege-star question as the decisive point requiring an answer. Principal limitation: Calling the renewed question a pseudo-problem does not provide a stable criterion separating empty iteration from a coherent rival standard, especially when the speaker acknowledges that the maneuver produces no evident progress. Live burden: The reply must explain why privileged normative facts legitimately terminate deliberation and why privilege-star fails to generate an equally intelligible practical demand. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects direct engagement with the central objection, explicit qualifications, and accurate representation, but also comparatively weak warrant and coherence where the crucial regress-blocking explanation is replaced by a contested label.

pro-comparative-alternative-burden.words: A difficulty shared by every plausible metanormative theory does not discriminate against realism unless a comparatively superior alternative handles it better overall.
pro-comparative-alternative-burden.critique: Strongest feature: The reply establishes a disciplined comparative standard, correctly observing that a challenge shared across remotely plausible metanormative positions cannot by itself select against realism, while the immediate retreat from an initially stronger formulation demonstrates unusually careful calibration. Principal limitation: The move does not independently establish that every plausible alternative inherits the same difficulty, and common failure would remove discriminatory force without showing that action-settling objectivity is an illegitimate requirement. Live burden: The argument must evaluate the proposed attitude-centered alternative and demonstrate either equivalent residual difficulties or offsetting costs in its account of ordinary objectivity. Locked score: The very strong band reflects excellent responsiveness, logical structure, representational fairness, and burden relevance, with the remaining limitation confined to evidential support for the universal comparative premise rather than the comparison's validity.

pro-limits-of-theoretical-guidance.words: Metaethical adequacy requires truth and plausibility, not an ability to extract every confused, mistaken, or skeptical agent from any residual practical uncertainty.
pro-limits-of-theoretical-guidance.critique: Strongest feature: The reply offers a principled methodological reframe by denying that metaethical adequacy requires universal therapeutic guidance for every mistaken or skeptical agent and substituting the more defensible constraints of theoretical truth and plausibility. Principal limitation: The skepticism analogy does not establish that the opponent's informed reflective cases are confused, and it risks weakening a challenge about promised action settlement into an excessive demand for persuading absolutely everyone. Live burden: The response must show why residual deliberation among informed agents is theoretically peripheral or explainable without abandoning realism's claimed connection between ought-conclusions and action guidance. Locked score: The strong and competent band rewards a coherent stopping principle, explicit scope, and meaningful subsidiary relevance, while recognizing reduced charity, limited analogical support, and incomplete contact with the central reflective counterexample.

pro-noncognitivist-objectivity-costs.words: An attitude-centered noncognitivism that preserves commonsense moral objectivity requires additional theoretical commitments whose plausibility and comparative cost must be assessed.
pro-noncognitivist-objectivity-costs.critique: Strongest feature: The objection directly restores the comparative burden omitted by a decision-centered alternative, insisting that structural proximity to action is not sufficient if preserving commonsense moral objectivity requires further semantic, psychological, or practical resources. Principal limitation: The source span neither inventories those additional commitments nor demonstrates that their combined cost exceeds realism's own ontological and deliberative commitments, leaving the claimed comparative disadvantage substantially programmatic. Live burden: The reply must specify what objectivity-preserving machinery noncognitivism needs and compare its explanatory performance against realism under common criteria rather than treating added structure itself as disqualifying. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects central relevance, appropriate conditional framing, and charitable openness about possible resources, tempered by evidential underdevelopment and a somewhat stronger cost implication than the supplied particulars warrant.

pro-first-person-deliberative-closure.words: When a first-person deliberator concludes that an action ought to be done, deliberation normally closes, although weakness of will may still prevent performance.
pro-first-person-deliberative-closure.critique: Strongest feature: The first-person test reaches the motion's action-guidance demand directly, cleanly distinguishing completion of deliberation from successful execution and expressly allowing both akrasia and variation in individual phenomenology. Principal limitation: Ordinary phenomenological closure does not itself establish that stance-independent facts non-causally settle every informed reflective dispute, particularly where an agent understands rival standards and experiences a substantive allegiance question. Live burden: The argument must explain why exceptional rival-framework cases do not reveal a structural gap, or else defend normal deliberative closure as the proportionate kind of objectivity realism promises. Locked score: The very strong band reflects outstanding motion relevance, precise qualifications, strong responsiveness, and a coherent experiential mechanism, while reserving room because its evidential base privileges ordinary first-person cases over the opponent's strongest informed counterexamples.

pro-centrality-weighted-theory-cost.words: Awkwardly accommodating rare reflective cases costs a theory less than failing to explain central features of ordinary normative and deliberative practice.
pro-centrality-weighted-theory-cost.critique: Strongest feature: The reply concedes rather than suppresses the reflective anomaly and introduces a useful comparative principle: explanatory awkwardness concerning exceptional cases may be less damaging than failure to capture central features of ordinary normative deliberation. Principal limitation: Centrality is asserted more than operationalized, and the response underdevelops the possibility that a rare foundational anomaly can expose a structural defect whose importance greatly exceeds its prevalence. Live burden: The proposed weighting method must distinguish explanatory centrality from mere familiarity and show why the rival-framework cases remain peripheral to the phenomenon realism claims to explain. Locked score: The very strong band recognizes high relevance, strong responsiveness, explicit concession, and proportionate calibration, while the remaining evidential and charitable limitations concern the justification of the comparative weights rather than the coherence of weighting costs.

pro-explanatory-not-contradictory-cost.words: The alleged deliberative gap is an explanatory imperfection rather than a contradiction, so its theoretical cost appropriately varies with the centrality of the affected phenomenon.
pro-explanatory-not-contradictory-cost.critique: Strongest feature: The response supplies a principled distinction between logical inconsistency and uneven explanatory naturalness, thereby explaining why localized awkwardness can be weighted by the centrality of the phenomenon whereas contradiction carries a different kind of theoretical liability. Principal limitation: The classification remains contestable because the opponent can treat contradictions as defeasible costs and argue that reflective anomalies disclose foundational explanatory damage rather than merely rough edges. Live burden: The argument must defend both the noncontradictory diagnosis and a principled measure of centrality capable of assigning substantial weight when an exceptional case genuinely transforms understanding. Locked score: The very strong band reflects clear conceptual structure, excellent direct responsiveness, strong burden relevance, and specific comparative support, tempered only by underdefended weights and the continuing possibility that the anomaly's foundational role has been understated.

strengths: Established a carefully qualified account of ordinary stance independence without pretending that discourse evidence alone completed the realist ontology.
Kept the exchange comparative by demanding that rival views demonstrate superior overall handling rather than merely identifying a difficulty potentially shared across theories.
Directly connected ought-judgment with first-person deliberative closure while clearly distinguishing completed deliberation from weakness of will or failed execution.
Conceded exceptional reflective anomalies and developed a coherent centrality-sensitive method for comparing their explanatory cost with failures concerning ordinary practice.
Repeatedly calibrated claims through explicit qualifications, including retreats from overstrong formulations and acknowledgment of phenomenological variation.

blunders.text: The rival-package replies repeatedly characterized iteration as a pseudo-problem without supplying the stable criterion needed to distinguish illegitimate repetition from a genuine higher-order practical question.
The indispensability argument compressed the bridge from usefulness in deliberation to ontological respectability, leaving the claimed parity with explanatory posits insufficiently defended.
The objection to noncognitivism invoked unspecified additional commitments, preventing a concrete comparison between those costs and realism's own theoretical commitments.

thesis.text: This AI-generated steelman, not transcript content or wording attributable to David Enoch, argues that stance-independent normative facts vindicate action-guiding objectivity when correctly grasped ought-judgments provide reasons whose authority does not require a further independent act of allegiance.

novelty.explanation: It integrates the pro route while explicitly repairing the missing bridge between realist facts, justified normative judgment, and deliberative closure.

premises.text: Ordinary moral judgment presents at least some reasons as answerable to features of conduct rather than to an agent's preferences, communal conventions, or contingent acceptance, creating a substantial explanatory demand for any adequate metanormative theory.

novelty.explanation: It develops the ordinary-stance claim into a comparative explanatory constraint without treating that constraint as a complete proof of realism.

premises.text: Deliberation necessarily treats some considerations as reasons bearing on what to do, and a theory that eliminates their truth-directed authority must explain how practical inquiry remains more than the organization of antecedently favored attitudes.

novelty.explanation: It strengthens the indispensability line by specifying the deliberative function whose theoretical replacement requires explanation.

premises.text: A justified first-person conclusion that one ought to perform an action normally ends the question of what reasons support, even though motivation may fail and unusual agents may reopen inquiry by challenging the conclusion's justification.

novelty.explanation: It preserves normal closure while accommodating informed reopening as a challenge to justification rather than an automatic second allegiance decision.

premises.text: Higher-order demands for choosing between every standard require a reason to believe that a genuine undefeated alternative remains; the mere formal possibility of constructing privilege-star does not establish an additional practical question.

novelty.explanation: It replaces the unsupported pseudo-problem label with an evidential condition for when iteration generates a live deliberative burden.

premises.text: Comparative assessment should weigh breadth, centrality, and severity separately, giving foundational anomalies serious attention without automatically allowing a rare explanatory imperfection to outweigh successful treatment of pervasive deliberative practice.

novelty.explanation: It operationalizes the centrality principle and answers the objection that rarity alone cannot determine theoretical importance.

conclusion.text: Robust realism therefore remains a proportionate account of normative objectivity if it explains stance-independent reasons, their indispensable deliberative role, and normal first-person closure better overall than alternatives while treating reflective anomalies as genuine but defeasible costs.

novelty.explanation: It draws a comparative and defeasible conclusion that is no stronger than the integrated premises support.

newArguments.title: The warranted-reopening distinction
newArguments.text: A residual question matters only when it is supported by a reason to doubt the operative ought-conclusion, not whenever an agent can grammatically ask what to do next. This distinguishes rational reopening from bare iterative questioning. Rival logical or normative frameworks can therefore matter when they expose an unresolved justificatory conflict, while invented privilege-star variants do not automatically create equal alternatives. Realism can acknowledge the former without accepting an endless allegiance requirement for every formally describable standard.

novelty.explanation: This new line supplies an independent criterion separating genuine reflective reopening from merely repeatable questioning.

newArguments.title: Multi-dimensional theoretical cost
newArguments.text: Theoretical costs should be compared along distinct dimensions: how frequently a phenomenon occurs, how central it is to the practice being explained, and how severely the theory misrepresents it. A rare case may be foundational and severe, so frequency cannot settle its weight; conversely, foundational interest does not guarantee that the alleged defect is destructive. This framework lets realism assign real weight to reflective anomalies while still defending its treatment of pervasive first-person deliberation against alternatives with broader objectivity costs.

novelty.explanation: This independently introduces a three-dimensional cost framework that refines the debate's simpler contrast between ordinary centrality and rare anomalies.

newArguments.title: Authority without motivational guarantee
newArguments.text: Action-guiding authority need not mean causal compulsion, guaranteed motivation, or immunity from renewed inquiry. A normative fact guides action when an agent who justifiably grasps it thereby has an answer to the question supported by reasons, even if weakness, distraction, or later evidence changes behavior. This interpretation preserves the distinction between settling what ought to be done and ensuring that it is done, while giving realism a clear standard against which an attitude-centered alternative must demonstrate superior explanatory coverage.

novelty.explanation: It repairs ambiguity about action settlement by separating rational authority, motivation, execution, and later justified reconsideration.
